# Ocr models

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_docs.py from the model cards; do not edit. -->

4 ocr models. Each section says what the model is, whether it may be used commercially and how fast it is; licences and checks are under Details.

Input: one RGB image. Output: the text lines in reading order: a quad `[N, 4, 2]` per line, its text and a confidence `[N]` (text detector + recogniser; recognisers alone read the whole image as one line).

Measured on RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130; `fastforks bench MODEL --size HxW` measures yours. The summary uses one input, 1080x1920: kernels time with its speed-up over the faster original run, and kernels peak reserved memory with its ratio to the smaller original one. Where measured (one variant per family), a variant's table also lists portable under `torch.compile` and the fp16 TensorRT engine of portable ([export](../export.md); memory: the engine's device memory + torch's peak). – = not measured; no kernels = the family has no kernels backend (reason under its table). Reserved memory is the allocator's cache: kernels (CUDA graphs, cuDNN workspaces) can reserve a few percent to some tens of percent more than portable at the same allocated peak.

Other devices: [Apple M1 Pro 16 GB](../devices/apple-m1-pro-16gb.md), [Apple M1 Pro 16 GB (MLX)](../devices/apple-m1-pro-mlx-16gb.md), [NVIDIA L4](../devices/l4-22gb.md), [NVIDIA L40S](../devices/l40s-44gb.md), [NVIDIA A10](../devices/a10-22gb.md), [NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB](../devices/a100-sxm4-40gb.md), [NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000](../devices/rtx-pro-6000-96gb.md); [across devices](../benchmarks.md#other-devices).

| model | commercial | kernels time (ms),<br>speed-up vs original | kernels peak memory (MiB, reserved),<br>ratio to original |
|---|---|---|---|

## PARSeq (scene text recognition)

PARSeq (Bautista and Atienza, ECCV 2022): reads one cropped word (Latin letters, digits, punctuation) with a Vision Transformer and a small decoder that refines its own guess; a base and a tiny version. Apache-2.0 code and weights.

Commercial use: yes.

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `parseq` | synthetic (32x128) | original (fp32)<br>original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 15.9<br>19.6<br>3.62<br>3.62<br>8.80<br>1.67 | 125 / 144<br>126 / 144<br>79 / 100<br>79 / 100<br>111 / 118<br>148 / 168 |
| `parseq-tiny` | synthetic (32x128) | original (fp32)<br>original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 14.6<br>18.0<br>2.10<br>2.10<br>1.54<br>1.67 | 56 / 58<br>56 / 58<br>44 / 54<br>44 / 54<br>76 / 94<br>82 / 90 |

### Measured

The 3,000 official cropped test words, with no lexicon. Exact accuracy and normalized edit similarity compare lowercase ASCII letters and digits. Similarity is one minus edit distance divided by the longer word's length, averaged over the crops. For a model that also detects text, this benchmark runs only its recognition network on the supplied word crop. Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.

| `parseq-tiny` | IIIT5K test (300 crops), word accuracy / normalized edit similarity % |  | 97.00 / 99.32 |  | 97.00 / 99.32 | 97.00 / 99.32 | 97.00 / 99.32 |  |

Measured on portable: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130, fastforks 535aedbb, 2026-11-19; portable32: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130, fastforks 3bf0bac7, 2026-11-18; kernels: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130, fastforks a54f74f7, 2026-11-19; compile: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130, fastforks 535aedbb, 2026-11-19; tensorrt: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130, fastforks 535aedbb, 2026-11-19.

## PP-OCRv5 (server / mobile)

PP-OCRv5 (Baidu, PaddleOCR 3, 2025): finds the text lines of a photo or document page in any orientation and reads them; Chinese (simplified and traditional), English, Japanese and pinyin; a server and a mobile version. Apache-2.0 code and weights.

Commercial use: yes.

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ppocrv5-server` | synthetic (1080x1920) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 762<br>277<br>235<br>277<br>25.1 | 2355 / 2901<br>1357 / 1452<br>1328 / 2708<br>958 / 1132<br>1131 / 1146 |
| `ppocrv5-mobile` | synthetic (1080x1920) | original (fp32)<br>original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 619<br>418<br>153<br>154<br>115<br>2.68 | 476 / 1094<br>393 / 1005<br>289 / 448<br>500 / 1016<br>292 / 448<br>241 / 268 |

### Limitations

- No document orientation / unwarping and no text-line orientation classifier (upside-down lines are read as they are).
- The DB post-processing runs on the CPU (OpenCV-exact geometry); hole contours of the binary map are not boxed (upstream boxes them too; they rarely pass `box_threshold`).
